title: Two-rescuer CPR with an AED: pads on during compressions, all clear for the shock
instruction: Do two-rescuer CPR with the AED on the manikin. With the right gripper closed, start chest compressions on the red mark within 10 seconds: repeated strokes from at least 3 cm above the mark down to within 1.5 cm of it, without pressing on the chest. Keep compressing while the left gripper puts one white pad flat on each blue square. Then both grippers stand clear, more than 5 cm from the manikin, while the AED analyses for 3 seconds; then press the orange shock button with the closed left gripper. Never touch the button while a gripper is near the manikin. Never pause compressions for more than 10 seconds before the shock; restart them within 3 seconds after it and keep them going.
context: Two-rescuer adult basic life support with an automated external defibrillator, as taught under the AHA and ERC resuscitation guidelines, is done by EMTs and paramedics (O*NET 29-2042, 29-2043), registered nurses (29-1141), lifeguards (33-9092) and workplace first-aiders. One rescuer keeps chest compressions going while the other attaches the AED's two pads (below the right collarbone, and on the left side below the armpit); compressions stop only when the AED analyses the rhythm; nobody may touch the patient during the analysis (movement corrupts it) or when the shock button is pressed (the shock can pass into a rescuer); the pause before the shock is kept under 10 seconds and compressions restart at once after it. Here the right gripper is the compressing rescuer and the left the AED operator. The scorer checks the whole sequence at every control step: who is touching the patient while the button is pressed, whether the pads went on while compressions continued, and how long compressions paused.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A CPR manikin stand-in lies face up across the table, its head toward +y (the robot's left), so the patient's right side faces the robot (-x) and the patient's left side faces away (+x). Nine things are on the table. (1) Manikin torso: a fixed skin-coloured rigid foam block standing in for an adult chest at about 0.7 scale, 240 mm along x (across the chest), 300 mm along y (shoulders at the +y end, waist at the -y end) and 50 mm tall, centred at x 20.5 cm, y -1.8 cm (it spans x 8.5 to 32.5 cm, y -16.8 to +13.2 cm), sides parallel to x and y. (2) Manikin head: a fixed skin-coloured rigid foam block 100 mm along x, 110 mm along y and 50 mm tall, centred at x 20.5 cm, y +19.7 cm (10 mm beyond the shoulders). (3) Compression mark: a red printed square, 30 x 30 mm and 1 mm thick, fixed on the torso's top, centred at x 20.5 cm, y -0.8 cm (the centre of the chest). (4) Sternal pad site: a blue printed square, 40 x 40 mm and 1 mm thick, fixed on the torso's top, centred at x 13.0 cm, y +10.2 cm (75 mm toward the patient's right and 110 mm toward the head from the compression mark: below the right collarbone). (5) Apex pad site: a blue printed square like it, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +1.2 cm (95 mm toward the patient's left and 20 mm toward the head: the left side of the chest in line with the armpit). (6) AED: a fixed yellow-green rigid plastic box, 100 x 100 x 45 mm, centred at x 42.0 cm, y +25.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. (7) Shock button: a fixed orange cylinder 30 mm across and 6 mm tall on the centre of the AED's top. (8) and (9) Two electrode pads: identical loose white firm-foam blocks standing in for a pad with its foam backing, 40 x 40 x 24 mm (24 mm tall), 15 g each, lying flat on the table beside the head, sides parallel to x and y, one centred at x 13.0 cm, y +28.5 cm and the other at x 28.0 cm, y +28.5 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads both pads and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (the point between its finger tips) and finger gap (94 mm fully open). Definitions. 'Closed': finger gap 30 mm or less. A 'compression' is counted when the right gripper, closed, with its finger-tip point within 20 mm of the compression mark's centre horizontally, comes down from at least 30 mm above the mark's top to 15 mm or less above it; before the next one counts it must go back up to 30 mm or more, closed over the mark (opening, or leaving the 20 mm, starts this over). Only the right gripper's compressions count. 'Compressions in progress': the right gripper closed, within 20 mm of the mark's centre and at most 45 mm above it, with a compression counted in the last 1.5 s. The gripper's heading is not read, so each gripper's fingers are taken as a stack of discs along the 38 mm from its finger-tip point back up the gripper, each reaching a finger's outer corner (half the finger gap plus 8 mm, and 13.5 mm across: 57 mm fully open, 21 mm closed). A gripper is 'at the patient' when any part of that zone is inside the box that extends 50 mm beyond the torso, or beyond the head, on every side seen from above, from the table up to 50 mm above that block's top; the area is 'clear' when neither gripper is at the patient. A pad is 'on its site' when it is tilted less than 10 degrees (either 40 x 40 mm face down), its lowest point is within 3 mm of the torso's top, and its centre is within 20 mm of the site's centre horizontally; the pads are identical, and either may go on either site. A pad 'went on during compressions' if compressions were in progress at the step it last arrived on a site. 'Pressing': a closed gripper's finger-tip point within 15 mm of the button's centre horizontally and at most 6 mm above the button's top. The AED: it analyses while both pads are on their sites and the area is clear; 3 s of that without a break completes an analysis and charges it (the charge is 'qualified' if, at that moment, both pads went on during compressions); any break restarts the analysis. A charge is cancelled when a pad leaves its site or a compression is counted. A press that began after the AED was charged and is held 0.5 s (10 control steps) delivers the shock, at that step; a press already under way when it charges does nothing. The AED delivers one shock per trial and does not analyse again after it. Pauses before the shock: the time from the trial's start to the first compression, every gap between compressions, and the time from the last compression to the shock (the pre-shock pause); the longest of these is the longest pause. After the shock: the post-shock pause is the time to the first compression, and compressions are 'kept up' for the time from that compression to the last of an unbroken run of compressions, each at most 1.5 s after the one before. Score 0 if, at any control step: a press of the shock button begins while the area is not clear (whether or not the AED is charged, before or after the shock); the area is not clear while a press that began on the charged AED is held, before the shock; a pad rests on the chest (lowest point within 5 mm of the torso's top) with its outline seen from above (its world-aligned bounding box) overlapping the compression mark; or a pad's lowest point is more than 10 mm below the table top (off the table). Otherwise: 1.0 if a shock was delivered from a qualified charge, the longest pause before it was at most 10 s, the post-shock pause was at most 3 s, compressions were kept up for at least 5 s, and both pads are on their sites with the left gripper not at the patient; 0.75 if a shock was delivered from a qualified charge but not all of the other 1.0 conditions are met; 0.5 if a qualified analysis was completed but no shock was delivered from a qualified charge; 0.25 if at some step both pads were on their sites at once; 0 in every other case (nothing done, compressions only, one pad, pads beside their sites). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both pads still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, no compression or press is seen, and the area counts as clear and the left gripper as not at the patient. In a real trial, a taped outline on the table 5 cm outside the manikin and a card standing beside it with lines at 5 cm above the manikin's top (and 15, 30 and 45 mm above the compression mark) are filmed from above and from the side; pad positions are read against the printed squares; a press is the closed fingers on the button cap (a touch sensor on the cap logs it); all times come from the video's or the sensor's timestamps.
reset_notes: Put both pads back flat on the table at x 13.0 cm, y +28.5 cm and x 28.0 cm, y +28.5 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Nothing is consumed: the pad stand-ins are reusable blocks, not adhesive pads; the manikin, marks and AED are fixed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. No force is simulated: a compression is a dip of the closed right gripper over the mark that stops short of the chest (the demo's hand stops 8 mm above it), because a real arm must not press on a hard torso; real compressions push the chest down 5 to 6 cm at 100 to 120 a minute, and neither depth nor rate is to scale (at least 15 mm of travel is required, and the demo compresses 46 times a minute). The AED is a model in the scorer: no heart rhythm, no voice prompts, a fixed 3 s analysis that charges at once, one shock; the scorer, not the device, sees who is at the patient. The pads are 40 x 40 x 24 mm blocks (real pads are about 12 x 10 cm and 2 mm thick, adhesive, with cables to the AED, none of which is simulated); the pad sites are printed squares the size of a pad. The manikin is a flat block torso at about 0.7 adult scale with a head block, no limbs or chest compliance; the apex site sits 2 cm higher on the chest than on a real chest so that the left arm reaches it without crossing the midline. 'Clear' concerns the grippers' fingers only, not the rest of each arm.
